incident_description:
We recently purchased the "Go Cat Teaser Cat Catcher Wand Cat Toy" from Petco, and our family enjoyed playing with our cat using the toy with no issues for the first couple weeks.  Then our 5 year old daughter was playing with the cat using the toy in our basement.  After about 5 minutes, some of the basement lights shut off unexpectedly, and our daughter said the cat toy broke.  I checked our home electrical panel and noticed the breaker tripped on one of the basement circuits.  Wondering what could have overloaded the circuit, I noticed the cover of one of the wall outlets was blackened as if from a small electrical fire.  We realized when our daughter was swinging the aforementioned cat toy around with its metal wire, it accidentally got wedged between the wall outlet and the plug of the electronic dartboard in our basement.  This caused a short circuit, a small electrical explosion at the wall outlet, and literally burned the wire of the cat toy in two.  Luckily our circuit breaker functioned as it should and cut power with no injury to our daughter.

We feel this cat toy should come with a warning that there is a shock hazard because of the metal wire, or at least a warning that it cannot be used by children without adult supervision.  We realize this was a freak occurrence and not every hazard needs a warning.  But it is not something that crossed our mind as parents, so we felt obligated to report this.
justification: The incident caused a short circuit and small electrical fire but no injury occurred.

incident_description: The BBC Grow and Discover Crystal Aquarium kit is marketed as a STEM activity for children.  It is composed of sodium metasilicate, which is dangerous dry and becomes a strong base (ph 12) when water is added.  There is a warning on the box, but the plastic aquarium is poorly designed with no lid, making it very easy to spill.  The product did spill in its entirety in our house, and my wife and I scrambled to sop it up before the strong base would destroy the varnish on our floors (the product insert says it will do so in 10 seconds of contact) and our electronics.  Needless to say we had no time to look for rubber gloves.  Both of us have very chapped skin on our hands, but thankfully none got in our eyes.  I am an ophthalmologist, and I know that a splash to the eye with a strong base like this with could be blinding.  It's entirely inappropriate to market this product to children (or anyone) without a serious revision of the aquarium design to reduce the very high risk of spilling the product.
justification: The incident resulted in chapped skin (injury) due to exposure to a strong base, and the product design makes spills likely.

incident_description: I bought OUT! Moisture Lock training pads for my dog.  The pads are folded in the package.  I went to place a pad down for my dog and shook it in the same manner you would shake a sheet or pillowcase to unfold it.  When I shook it, the end burst open (or was not sealed properly in the first place) and I was sprayed in the eyes with the product inside (little pellets).  The pellets stuck to my eyes and it began to burn and I was not able to see clearly.  I began to flush my eyes while my husband consulted the package for information regarding ingestion or contact with eyes and the package said nothing.  I called the question/comment line listed on the package.  The incident happened before their normal business hours and their message told me to call CHEMTREC in case of a medical emergency.  I called the number on the message and the man who answered said that they were not medical professionals and to call poison control.  The woman at poison control was able to tell me that the product contained ammonia and alcohol and that eye irrigation was needed.  After sufficiently irrigating my eyes, my eyes were fine although they burned for several hours and I developed a headache.  My concern is the absence of warning information on the package about ingestion or contact with eyes.  The only warning on the package was a suffocation warning about the plastic packaging.  I was also concerned about the company I was told to call in case of a medical emergency that was not able to help me.
justification: The incident resulted in eye irritation and a headache, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the product's design and lack of warnings.

incident_description: While changing my whole-home water filter I leaned my arm on my Olympic Kiln and got shocked (240V-1 phase). I investigated, first checking my home wiring then checked the kiln. I found that there was an open limit to ground. Although the kiln is still under warranty, I opened the plug (a large 240V plug) and found that the ground wire was not attached. The kiln is wired using liquid tight conduit as a power cord. From my research, I don't think that is up to code. It also has a four prong plug but only three of the prongs are connected. I also discovered that the kiln bears a UL Listed label but the product doesn't appear in the UL directory (these items were reported to UL). I contacted the Olympic Kilns. They want me to reattach the ground wire on the plug. They would not address the other concerns I had about the conduit and the plug. I am concerned that someone could get killed. I am lucky that I leaned on the kiln and the electricity pushed me away. If I had grabbed the kiln, I may have been drawn to it. I think that Olympic Kilns may be manufacturing products that are not up to NEC (National Electric Code). What I found in the NEC section 422.43 (b) sounds like conduit is not allowed as a power cord. I wasn't able to find out if using only three prongs of a four prong plug is code compliant. I don't know where to go to make them produce safe consumer products.
justification: The incident resulted in an electric shock, which is an injury, and there are concerns about potential fatal outcomes due to the kiln's wiring issues.

incident_description:
I am submitting this report to raise awareness and seek immediate investigation into the Tidy Cats Breeze Cat Litter Pellets, manufactured and sold by Purina, due to severe and life-threatening health risks posed by this product. The product, containing Modernite Zeolite as the main ingredient, has been linked to numerous cases of serious illnesses and death in cats, as well as potential health risks to humans. 

 Summary of Health Concerns: 
 1. Harm to Cats:
  Several verified reviews on Amazon and other platforms have documented cases of cats ingesting these litter pellets, leading to critical health issues including severe non-regenerative anemia, kidney failure, heart failure, and death. 
  In my personal experience, one of my cats ingested the Tidy Cats Breeze pellets and subsequently became gravely ill. X-rays revealed that his abdomen was filled with the pellets, which do not dissolve in water, making them impossible to pass naturally. 
  Cats that ingest these pellets or lick their paws after using the litter are at risk of ingesting toxic substances released by the product. These substances have been linked to catastrophic health outcomes. 

 2. Documented Cases and Evidence: 
  Online reviews, social media groups, and direct outreach from other consumers highlight that my case is not isolated. Numerous cat owners have reported similar outcomes, with many cats succumbing to illness despite medical intervention. 
  Published articles have drawn connections between zeolite, the primary component of these pellets, and various health issues in animals, including cancer, anemia, and organ failure. 

 3. Risks to Humans: 
 The dust generated by this litter poses serious health risks to humans, particularly pregnant women, children, and babies, who may inhale or come into contact with the dust. 
  Given the widespread use of this product in households, the potential human exposure to the harmful effects of zeolite through inhalation or ingestion is concerning. 

 Purinas Response: 
  When I contacted Purina regarding my cats illness caused by the ingestion of these pellets, they offered to cover my veterinary bills, but only under the condition that I sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA). I refused to sign the NDA, as it became evident that Purina is aware of the risks posed by this product and has attempted to suppress information regarding the harm it causes. 
  Despite numerous complaints from consumers, Purina continues to sell the product, seemingly prioritizing profit over the well-being of pets and consumers. 

 Financial and Emotional Impact: 
  I have personally incurred thousands of dollars in veterinary bills trying to save my cat in 2022. Many other pet owners have reported similar financial burdens, while some have lost their pets altogether. 
  The emotional toll on families who have lost their beloved pets to this dangerous product is immeasurable.

 Call to Action: 
  I urge the Consumer Product Safety Commission to investigate Purinas Tidy Cats Breeze Cat Litter Pellets and consider enforcing a recall due to the products toxicity. 
  It is imperative that proper labeling and warnings are provided regarding the severe health risks associated with the use of this litter. 
  Furthermore, the Commission should look into potential violations of consumer safety regulations, especially considering Purinas knowledge of the harm and their attempts to silence affected consumers with NDAs. This product continues to pose a serious threat to both cats and humans, and immediate action is necessary to prevent further harm.
justification: The description reports numerous cases of severe illness and death in cats, as well as potential health risks to humans, indicating a high severity level and likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I had a marineland Stealth aquarium heater, I believe it was a ETP 150.  In January ago I noticed that the top had "popped off".  I was concerned about electrocution, so I unplugged the unit.  When I removed it from the tank, there was a strong smell of burning plastic coming from the unit.

Since then I have replaced that unit with another, I will now be contacting the manufacturer for a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning aquarium heater with no reported injury, but potential for harm was present.

incident_description: Comfort Zone pheromone  diffuser for cats #100532987.   Within 3 hours of plugging it in, we noticed a burning smell in our home and after searching for all of the obvious kitchen & bathroom suspects, I thought to look at the diffuser.  The body of the diffuser was extremely hot requiring me to use a glove to remove it from the outlet.  After 30 minutes of being unplugged, the smell dissipated.  I am returning the diffuser to Amazon which, after reading the reviews post purchase, demonstrates that MANY other people have had the same issue.   I emailed the company directly but after seeing the number of complaints on Amazon believe that it is a true safety hazard.   I believe that if we hadnt been home to unplug the diffuser, a fire was a real possibility.
justification: The diffuser overheated and emitted a burning smell, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: Woke up to the smell of something burning. Found the "pet safe" heating pad burning itself, the couch and the pet bed.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a heating pad, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I checked the temperature on my saltwater aquarium as I do every morning, and the temperature had spiked to over 95 degrees, I unplugged and removed the heater from the tank, but it was too late, my corals and my oyster died. : (
justification: The incident resulted in the death of marine life but no human injury or death.

incident_description:
We used InkBird thermostats to control our reptile enclosures.  Over the past few months we have had three of their devices fail.  The failure was the exact same on all devices.  Details:
- Devices were set to maintain a temperature of 88 degrees Fahrenheit
- The devices lost control and caused the heat pads to reach 102, 115, and 140 (where we caught the separate temperatures for the three failed devices).
- The device probe was accurately reading the high temperatures but wasn't doing anything to control it.

We were home for the first two failures and caught them in time but we were out for the evening for the third failure.  It reached temperatures high enough to melt plastic in the enclosures and unfortunately killed 5 of our geckos.

All three devices failed shortly after their two year date of purchase.  We were not even close to using the total wattage that the devices are rated for.  We were in fact only using less than a third of their rated capacity.  All were on separate circuits in the house.

I emailed InkBird to notify them and their solution was to attempt sending me  a new device and couldn't have cared less.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of 5 geckos due to thermostat failure, indicating a severity level of 4 (Death). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as there were three failures within a short period under similar conditions.

incident_description:
we had a marineland stealth pro heater in our 90 gallon aquarium, that exploded today, Aug.7 2011
the heater shattered, killing most of the fish, and sending burnt glass all over the aquarium and water out of the top of the tank.  everything in the tank was damaged, and it has taken over 12 hours to try to empty the tank.  everything needs replacement.  we needed to purchase a temporary tank and supplies, and will need to completely re do the original tank, fuses were blown in the home. we are only lucky our home did not catch fire.  the tank is destroyed, fish are dead, our carpets are soaked, and needless to say, we are very upset.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and killed the fish, but no human injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We have a 3-gallon Eclipse acquarium. One night, it started to smell like something was burning. When we went into the kids' room, we found that the top (where the motor and the light are housed) was melting.  Literally nothing had changed from the days before when we had it running.  It just seems to have overheated and burned the plastic housing.  A total fire hazard. Thank god we were home and not out at the time.
justification: The aquarium's motor and light housing melted, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was gifted a Heyby cat tree tower. It states it is safe for kittens and cats. I rescued a 1-year-old cat and also have a small 5-year-old cat. The tree was put together properly. On 10/20/2023 one of my cats was sleeping on the top bed on the tree and my other in the peep hole bed. At 5am the tree fell and hit the wall and my cats were thrown off.  My small cat has been so scared she is hiding. I place the cat tree in the middle of the living room, and it fell again hitting a 3 shelve wall unit. Only one cat was on it. THIS IS DANGEROUS! Not only are my cats afraid but it broke my wall unit. It is not fit for 2 cats or maybe just one. I am lucky it did not fall on my glass table. CUSTOMERS NEED TO BE WARNED OF THE DANGER. My cat that was sleeping on the top had a small limp but she is okay now my scared to come in the room.
justification: The cat tree fell multiple times, causing a minor injury (limp) to one cat and scaring the other, but no serious harm occurred.

incident_description:
In December I purchased the Kids Made Modern Stamp Set at Target. Today my kids and I went to use the stamp pads for a project and found what appears to be mold growing on them. I have attached 3 pictures of the pads with the growth on them so you can see what I mean.

I would suggest that this product be recalled and all stamp pads made by this brand re-evaluated. Luckily I was with my children so I could keep them from touching the pads, but other kids might get closer or want to touch them to see what it is.
justification: No injury occurred, but mold on the stamp pads poses a potential health risk if touched, especially by children.

incident_description: My daughter's 60 pound Australian Shepherd's head got stuck between the bars of pet gate. I was at home, and I was able to bend the bars apart to free him. The manufacturer photos of the gate show a child with a dog. I found out that the spacing between the bars is 2-1/2".  I discovered that the vertical bars aren't rigid, since I was able to bend them with my hands. This gate does not meet baby gate standards, yet the manufacturer photo shows a child next to the gate.
justification: The dog was stuck but freed without injury, and the gate's design poses a risk but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description: Stealth aquarium heater, Model ETP50-50W Using it to heat fish tank. Malfunctioned, shut off and killed my fish. It then caught fire.
justification: The heater malfunction caused property damage (fish death and fire) but no human injury or death.

incident_description: My child was playing in her playpen with her Dora the explorer camera contest book. I then heard her throw up. I picked her up and she threw up quite violently 4 more times. On the last time, I realized there was a piece of plastic, almost like a laminate or a clear wrapper. I put her down and checked in the playpen to see what on earth it was and realized there was more laminate pieces laying in there. I picked them all out and then went through her toys and realized it was the dora book. It was coated in a laminate film but on the front where there is a cutout for a toy camera it wasn't secure allowing her to peel pieces of film off. I now realize the vomiting first started out with her choking and gagging which was what alerted me to pick her up. Some of the pieces were large and could have easily cut off her airway. I pealed the rest of the film off of the book and it covered both the front and the back of the book and was relatively easy to peel off.
justification: The child vomited and choked on plastic film, indicating a potential choking hazard but no lasting injury occurred.

incident_description: Removed Dog Bell from home electrical outlet and only one electrical prong remained attached to the device.  The other electrical prong remained in the electrical outlet, shorting the electrical outlet and tripping the circuit breaker.
justification: The incident caused a short circuit but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The heater was placed in 55 gallon tank, 2 years ago. She noticed that the fish began swimming erratically. The temperature the heater was placed on was 78 degrees but the temperature in the tank went up to 92 degrees with the heater set at 78.  A seperate thermometer is kept in the aquarium.

She touched the side of the tank and it was hot to the touch. She noticed that twenty two of the fish had died. She unplugged the heter to allow it to cool off before removing the fish. She removed the heater from the tank and throws it out in the garbage. It was then replaced with another model from the same firm. 

She contacted the retailer and they advised her that they were aware of other consumers experiencing the same failure with the tank. A few days later she noticed there was a recall online (Release #11-202). The heater I which she was currently using was also affected by the recall. The firm is going to send out the repair kit but she has also disconintued using the heater.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of fish but no human injury, and the retailer acknowledged similar failures, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: I recently bought an American Craft Lazer Square. Shortly after inserting the 9v battery in each arm I noticed, upon picking it up, that the one arm was extremely hot. My husband opened the battery compartment & smoke poured out. The casing around the battery had melted as well as one of the wires. I have called and written this company as I was extremely concerned with the SAFETY of others unsuspecting to this. Had I not noticed this would have been in my craft room & most likely would have burnt down my home with us in it. This company emailed me back telling me they understood my frustration. I found it a bit more serious that frustrating. Despite my several emails nobody asked for the sku or any information on the product. My final correspondence I did tell them of my intent to contact this agency and then & only then did they disclose that they were aware & their lab is investigating it. To date they have nothing on my particular piece. I would like this report filed in the case that a fire is started and there is property & or human life lost.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning product that caused overheating and smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Mophorn Heat Press 5 in 1 Multifunction Sublimation Heat Press Machine Desktop Iron Baseball Hat Press 1400W Digital Swing Away Transfer T Shirt Hat Mug (5IN1) on Amazon thru Mophorn in September 2016. I have used it maybe 20-30 times and Starting in February when I used it sparks flew out the back of the machine. The first time it happened I thought it was a fuse that blew. I cleaned the machine "fixed" the fuse and tried it again and thats when the blew my breaks sparks/flames flew out the back and it shut off. It now turns on again and heats up but I refuse to use it. I have spoken to a number of people with this heat press and they had the same incident happen to them.
justification: Sparks and flames indicate a hazardous incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Pet bed warmer became BURNING HOT on first use.  Almost burned my hand.  My hand was stinging for about an hour.   Unplugged immediately, could have burned my dog.  I set it up as directed, under a layer of bedding.  Many reports of animal burns on Amazon in regards to this product.  It must be removed from public!
justification: The incident caused injury (hand stinging for an hour) and posed a risk of severe harm to the dog, with multiple reports of animal burns.

incident_description: A reptile heating pad caught fire inside an enclosure.
justification: The heating pad caught fire, indicating an incident occurred, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Purchased a new Petnova CatGenie litter box 3 years ago. It caught on fire in our home on 11/1/24. We were home at the time, so my husband unplugged it and put it out. Its just over 3 years old, never gets used, its only plugged in for the *never* occasion that the other two boxes our 3 cats actually use are occupied. We run a cleaning cycle bi-weekly so the water doesnt stagnate, but the box is otherwise unused and in pristine condition. I called the customer support number on CatGenie.com and told the rep the events and she sounded SHOCKED, saying Ive never heard of that before! Ill escalate this to management right away!! And said the words It couldnt have caught on fire. Its designed not to. I finally get a call back 3 hours later. The resolution I was offered was to ship it back free of charge, and they could repair it for $250. She said thats all she can offer. Turns out, theres a significant number of people reporting the same issue on several social media platforms. This isn't a warranty issue, its a safety recall issue. My home still smells like burnt plastic throughout and were lucky thats our biggest concern
justification: The litter box caught fire but no injuries were reported, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description:
Love this little iron for my sewing and crafting projects, BUT this iron gets way too hot...it could have burned the house down.  It was accidentally left on for several hours and managed to burn through the cord, the cutting mat, and the wooden cutting table!  The little flimsy stand that goes with it is not adequate.  The protective barrel also does not work as intended since the heated tip is weighted and the iron tips past the protective covering.  Mine did not come with a heat sleeve, although I think they may now be available separately.

I have sent an email and photos to the manufacturer asking them to consider some safety options.  Yes, I know I need to be more careful, but truthfully -- how many crafters have not forgotten to cut something off occasionally?  My curling iron, my home iron, et al. all have auto shutoff.  I am willing to pay extra for this.  I will be buying a separate auto-off plug now for my glue gun, etc. but folks need to be warned about how hot this thing actually gets...it can do some serious damage.  

I have photos but could not paste into this text block.
justification: The iron caused property damage but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I don't think there has been an injury, although I will have my children tested for lead exposure.  In the most recent PIRG report, I found that the book "Little Hands Love" by Piggy Toes Press, has more than twice the allowable 300 ppm lead levels (I think those levels have been dropped). I have been reading this book to my children for the last year to two years. Although PIRG shows the book in its report, this book is STILL AVAILABLE for purchase on many websites, including the manufacturer's website.  This should not be allowed.
justification: No injury reported, but potential lead exposure from a book still available for purchase constitutes an incident.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he smelled an odor of electric fire and discovered that the aquarium heater was sparking and cracked open, this caused fatality to his fishes and corals.  He was not aware what was causing the problem, so it took him several hours to figure out that it was caused from the heater to eventually unplug it.

Consumer stated that this incident is estimated at a damage of $3,000. He had experienced similar problems of Release #11-202.

12/5/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised to send in the report of damages which included all documentation and proof to this incident.
justification: The incident caused property damage (aquarium heater and marine life) but no human injury or death.

incident_description: Tore open a book cover to a extremely sharp aluminum sheet. Approximately 4in x 9in. With extremely sharp edges
justification: The description mentions a sharp aluminum sheet but does not indicate any injury occurred.

incident_description:
There are items on e-bay geared towards pet owners.  While it might seem fun to a consumer it is dangerous to the pet.  These laser pointers one in particular FroliCat Bolt Automatic Laser Light Teaser Toy has an adjustable mirror which can allow a consumer to tilt the laser to the point of getting the laser into the pet's eyes.  These lasers are dangerous to sight.  They can blind an animal or human if these lasers are directed directly towards an eye.  These can be used unattended.  While the cat may chase the point of light many kittens and older cats will look to see where the light is coming from.  I know my cats are smart and especially the one of mine who jumps on our printer to try to see how the paper travels in the front and comes out the front.  She always tries to figure out how it turns the paper around.

These should be removed from the market before someone or someone's pet gets really hurt.
justification: The description highlights a potential for eye injury to pets or humans from laser pointers, indicating a risk of injury if misused.

incident_description: NAFD Engine 2 was dispatched to the address for a mattress fire that was already out, but the home owner wanted us to make sure. A  child had taken some hampster bedding out of a pet toy and while playing with it on her bed near a lit candle on her nightstand. The bedding came into close proximity of the candle and it ignited. It was dropped on the bed where it caught the bed spread and mattress on fire. No injuries reported.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I had a Marineland Stealth Pro 250W ML90453-00 literally explode in my 75gal aquarium. This killed 2ea Brilliant Blue Diamond and 1ea Mandarin Orange Discus, 6ea Skunk Cory and 3ea Siamese Algae Eaters. The concussion broke a glass cover and airstone. I have pictures and replacement costs if required.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage and loss of aquatic life, but no human injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased NITE IZE NITE HOWL LED SAFETY NECKLACE in the winter of 2020-2021. It's a dog collar that is charged by 3 lithium button batteries. I only used them about a handful of times and just last week noticed that the lights were very dim, so I went to replace the button batteries and upon opening the back, I saw that 2 of the 3 batteries was extremely swollen. I changed the batteries and left the old ones on top of our 3D printer. A few hours later, as I was talking on the phone with a good friend and walking past our 3D printer, I heard what sounded like a gunshot, a huge POP right as I walked past. After I collected my thoughts and verified that i was not hit and that all my windows were in tact, I noticed one of the button batteries had exploded in 3 different locations about my dining room and hallway to my kitchen. Then I noticed 2 different walls that were located next to pieces of the button batteries were damaged by this explosion. It had exploded with such force that it took off paint and made a huge indentation in my kitchen wall and also threw another piece directly into my dining room wall. Luckily, the explosion just merely missed hitting me! If I had not took those batteries out of the collars, 100% they would have exploded and killed my dogs! These should be taken off the shelves at once to prevent this from happening to a sweet innocent pet. I've purchased this from the store Petpeople in Aurora, IL but I'm aware that they are on sale as well currently on [REDACTED], [REDACTED], [REDACTED], [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and list goes on. People need to be aware. I've just read a review from an [REDACTED] customer thar purchased this same product that this has happened to as well. And with their situation, the collars back (that is actually held on by a single screw) had gotten blown off during the explosion and broke the back into several pieces. Luckily for them, it was also not on their dog at the time of explosion.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Marineland Stealth Aquarium Heater: ETP150-150 watts:  I have had the heater for a couple of years. The heater has always been set at 75 degrees F, and never moved.  Last week I noticed that my corals were all limp.  I checked the tank temp and it was at 86 degrees F.  I unplugged the heater, let it cool down and removed it. I iced the tank to slowly bring down the temp.  I replaced it with another Marieland Stealth EPT-250-250 watts which I have as a back up (I have three Marineland Stealth heaters in all).  Today, while at my local fish store I wanted to by another one and was told that there had been a recall and that I should check out Marinelands website. He told me that I should remove all three heaters.  I did.
The Marienland site had your link (disabled!), so I did a search and found that you would still like input.
Now that I have read that there may be over 1 million of them out there, I am bothered that the retail distributers were not bound to post this recall/"warning" on their front door where all their customers could see it.  
Thank you.   [redacted]
justification: The heater malfunction caused a temperature spike, damaging corals but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Amazing Baby Feel and Learn soft toy book has a [REDACTED] string attached with 2 plastic rings.  This is a baby item for infants.  6 month old daughter was playing with this and got the string completely wrapped around her neck.  Luckily she was being supervised and we were able to get it off of her and she did not get strangled.  This could potentially have been a very serious situation.  This item is sold on the internet and sold by the company amazing baby.  They should not sell baby toys that have strings attached as this could pose a strangulation risk.  It is sold at many retailers as well.
justification: The string wrapped around the baby's neck but no injury occurred due to supervision.

incident_description: I  bought a Top Fin 5.5 Gal Aquarium Starter Kit,  Item: 36-5166072 at pet smart almost six months ago. last week the LED lighting started to turning off coming back on  until went off. the problem is the LED case started to get hot, eventually got melted and also the cover where the LED attach got melted. I haven't see it until I was cleaning  the aquarium couple days after the light went off. when the light went off I decide to turn off the switch off, which  was the best I did since I did didn't knew the LED case and the hood was melting. the LED case is not seal for water condensation.  I just want to  prevent from something worse.
justification: The LED lighting malfunction caused melting of the case and cover, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Returned home from a 4 day vacation to an overwhelming smell that something had burnt (burning/chemical smell).  Upon searching, I found that the Stealth Pro fish tank heater (model ML90453 - 250watt) in my 90 gallon tank had apparently exploded and several of my very expensive cichlids were dead.  There was debris all over the tank (black plastic and black unknown substance).  I was VERY FORTUNATE that the tank didn't break or the explosion didn't result in a fire.   I'm not sure exactly when this occurred but from the look of my dead fish, it happened within a day or two prior to my returning home.
justification: The fish tank heater exploded, causing damage and dead fish, but no human injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I have 9 turtle aquariums that have all been using the Stealth Pro underwater heathers for approximately 1 year or just a little less. About 2 months ago, one of my 75 gallon tanks way overheated during the night. The turtle that lives in that tank is an approximately 7 water turtle. The water temperature in all my turtles tanks was normal when I turned off their lights for the night. (I check everything in all the tanks both morning & night to make sure all is OK.)The next morning when I turned on his lights he jumped off his basking platform into the water immediately began swimming back & forth frantically. Luckily I saw him do that & went to get him out to see what was wrong. During the night his water felt like it had heated to almost boiling. Luckily he spent the night out of the water on his basking platform. I was shocked when I put my hand in to get him. It scared me to think how long he was actually in that extremely high water temperature.
justification: The turtle was exposed to extremely high water temperature but was not injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I watched a video of an automatic self-cleaning cat litter box with a potentially lethal design. Unlike other self-cleaning machines, this design rotates on the y-axis and closes on the opening (fixed to the base) during the cleaning cycle.  The anti-pinch sensors are faulty, which has resulted in two cats being trapped and crushed to death. It's only a matter of time before a baby or child gets injured or killed. This video explains the horrific design and these shady companies in more detail: [REDACTED].

The machines are sold under various company names across platforms such as Amazon, Wayfair, and Walmart in several countries.  The man who created the video has compiled a list of all the listings of automatic self-cleaning litter boxes he could find that use this design: [REDACTED]
justification: The description reports two cats being crushed to death due to faulty anti-pinch sensors, indicating a severity level of 4 (Death). The widespread availability and faulty design suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Bought the Top Fin Aquarium Heater HT150 approximately 6 months ago. Product worked fine up until a couple days ago. The water in my tank was low and i went to add water, I noticed that approximately 7 of my fish had perished. I felt the water. It was extremely warm. I checked the heater and the green light was on. I pulled the heater out of the tank and it nearly burnt my fingers. I dropped the obviously malfunctioning unit in the sink to cool. There is a recall for the product. I will return it to the store.
justification: The incident resulted in fish death due to a malfunctioning heater, but no human injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was changing the water in my 75 gallon aquarium.

I pulled the filter cartridge from my filter and the electric shock staggered me.  Thinking it was the filter, I unplugged it and attempted to remove the cartridge.  I was again staggered from the shock.  Since the heater was the only other electric appliance in contact with the water I unplugged it and no more electric shock.  I plugged the filter back in and no more shock.

A GOOGLE search revealed a product recall.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock from an aquarium heater, which caused the person to be staggered but did not result in any reported injury.

incident_description: We have had the heater for about 2 and 1/2 months. I stuck my hand in the fish tank and got shocked. Nothing is broken on it or cracked.
justification: The description mentions getting shocked, which implies an injury occurred.

incident_description: I own a several VIPARSPECTRA Timer Control Dimmable 300w LED Aquarium Light Full Spectrum for Grow Coral Reef Marine Fish Tank purchased from amazon that I have hanging over my salt water fish tanks.  While adjusting the light with the lights off, but plugged in, I received an electric shock and my finger was numbed when it touched one of the external side screws.  I then used a digital multimeter and set at 20 DCV and was able to register a current that kept fluctuating between 0.00 and 0.08.  I have 3 other lights that I tested and found this to be an issue with 1 other light.
justification: The incident resulted in an electric shock causing numbness, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The issue was found in 2 out of 4 lights tested, indicating a possible occurrence likelihood.

incident_description: My 1 year old daughter was playing with those viral busy books. I got one from Amazon that was specifically listed for 1 year olds and older. She was playing with the book and the zippers came right off. I was able to get to her in time before any drastic happened!
justification: The zippers came off the book, posing a choking hazard, but no injury occurred as the parent intervened in time.

incident_description:
On July 1, 2020 time 5:30 pm, I took my  60 lb. Golden Retriever dog out for her usual afternoon walk.  

For the last 3-4 years, I have been using the Pet Smart brand gentle-lead collar.  My dog will lunge at small animals expecially cats, and for the last 3-4 years this product has controlled her head and prevented injury to me by doing what it proclaims.  This product was recommended and fitted by my vet.
On July 1, 2020 my dog lunged at a cat.  This time, the Pet smart gentle-lead did not control her face/head and she pulled me down a driveway.  As she dove under a truck to get the cat, I slammed my head, torso and hips into a parked truck tailgate.  I was transported by ambulance to a nearby emergency room where I was diagnosed with a concussion to the forehead, possible retina detachment, fracture to my optical orbital floor and fracture of nose bridge, possible hairline fracture to ribs, focal hematoma to hip bone, 26 stitches to my face and 9 staples on my scalp, nerve damage to my left hand because I tried to brace for impact. Not to mention scrapes and bruises to both knees.

I don't want anyone else to get a false sense of safety by using this product!
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including fractures, a concussion, and nerve damage, requiring emergency medical treatment.

incident_description:
I purchased Tidy Cats Lightweight  litter. It was very very dusty. It left a plume of heavy dust throughout my bedroom where the litter box is. My heathy cat quickly developed a bad cough, she has a cloudiness in her lungs and is diagnosed with respiratory infection and dies. Soon after Im in the hospital with respiratory issues and low blood platelets and I almost die. I needed to have my spleen removed and Im in I C U at UCLA for weeks. I had not been breathing well since.  I started cleaning up my bedroom of this fine cat litter dust and then my breathing becomes worse and  I cannot breathe at all. I go to my local hospital where I receive. CT scan of my lungs, chest X-ray and EKG.  Doctors confirmed that I too have the cat litter dust in my lungs.  I have read a lot of bad reviews on this product recently and consumers have been complaining for years about this product and it has also killed cats, Im lucky it didnt kill me. Please, please look into this product. It is a hazard to pets and people!!!
My doctors are also filing this warning with the Consumer Product Safety Board.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a cat and severe respiratory issues in a human, requiring hospitalization and medical intervention.

incident_description:
We purchased 4 16 oz tubs of Speedball "Speedy Kids" Washable Fingerpaint in fall 2010 at Pearl Art in San Francisco when the store was going out of business. We didn't open the paints until today. Three tubs were sealed with a double-layer seal imprinted with the words "sealed for freshness." Those three tubs were fine. The fourth was sealed only with a thin foil seal. The paint was chunky and had a foul odor than made us nauseated quickly (both my 4-year-old daughter and me). We closed it back up and decided we would not use it at all.

I have also reported this to the manufacturer, Speedball Arts.
justification: The foul odor caused nausea in both the child and the adult, indicating a minor health impact.

incident_description: The bowl is stainless steel and has prongs to make the dog slow down when eating.  The instructions indicate that the prongs should be removed and washed.  When I attempted to unscrew the prong, the prong edge sliced my finger open.  I  notified the company that sells the bowl of the danger but they are still selling the product.
justification: The prong edge caused a finger injury, which fits severity level 3 (Injury). The likelihood is possible (3) as the product is still being sold without modification.

incident_description: Grreat Choice Fragrance Free Cat Litter - I have bought this product several times in the last several months. I bought three 40 pound boxes on 3/1/16. One box was used to fill a litter box and I had an immediate severe reaction of feeling of burning in my lungs, sore throat, congestion, lethargy, and a general not well feeling even long after I left the environment. I have a severe fragrance allergy. This type of reaction only happens with highly fragranced products. The product is very obviously fragranced and not fragrance free as labeled on the package. This product is dangerous to people with fragrance or chemical allergies. I have had to wear a mask inside my home. The product is being removed and the environment cleaned today.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Hyper Pet Duck sling shot toy from Cabela's.  After carefully reading the instructions on the package, I went outside to play with the toy with one of my Golden Retrievers.  Upon the third time of pulling back the toy, the slingshot apparatus inside completely broke.  The metal piece inside sliced open my hand, forcing me to have 4 stitches put in at the base of my thumb.
justification: The slingshot broke and caused a hand injury requiring stitches, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is possible (3) as the toy failed during normal use.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the circular rim of the helping magnifier he purchased is very sharp. The consumer has bought 3 of these products from the retailer. The consumer's daughter cut her right index finger when she tried to remove the protective plastic from the magnifier, resulting in a her applying a band aid. She did not go to the doctor nor seek medical attention. The product is a manual tool. The incident occurred as soon he presented product to his daughter and she tried to open the product. The consumer has yet to call the retailer about the product but does intend to return two of the magnifiers. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer about this incident. 

Update:  Consumer returned all 3 back to the recently opened Braintree store on Aug 09, 2011 (store #351)  (Copy of return receipt enclosed)

incident_description:
Upon ordering and receiving this product I have learned that this product does not comply with the standards outlined in the GHS (Globally Harmonized System). This poses significant risks to consumer health and safety and violates the Fair Packaging and Labeling Act 15 U.S.C.  1451-1461

The product does not contain the 6 essential elements of compliance.

Product packaging does not contain 
1. Name, Address and Telephone Number
2. Product Identifier
3. Signal Word
4. Hazard Statement(s)
5. Precautionary Statement(s)
6. Pictogram(s)
 

This product is also in violation of the following mandatory standards 
15 U.S.C. 2063(a)(5)  Product Certification and Labeling (Tracking Labels)
16 CFR 1110 Certificates of Compliance
16 CFR 1700 Poison Prevention Packaging
FHSA (Federal Hazardous Substances Act)
PPPA (Poison Prevention Packaging Act) - Packaging is not child-proof.
justification: The product's non-compliance with safety standards poses significant health and safety risks, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description: A child's easel was purchased for my son's second birthday. The legs broke within a couple weeks and it was typically used laying flat on the living room floor to doodle on. My 8 month old daughter would crawl onto the chalkboard surface while my son was drawing and touch it. At my daughter's 9 month well visit they do a routine veinous lead test. She tested a 30 and has lead poisoning. The county health department came to inspect our apartment and found that the chalkboard surface of the easel was the source of the lead. We only had the product for 2 months and that brief exposure was enough to poison her.
justification: The child suffered lead poisoning from the easel's chalkboard surface, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: Today my daughter who is almost 5 opened her Ada Twist  Go and Glow  light up Journal to show me her drawing and it pinched the skin of her arm in the binding/hinge of the book. It was really scary and has left a huge mark. I know she'll be fine but I feel this product should be taken off the shelf and redesigned. We had purchased it at our local Walmart probably about a month ago or less.

incident_description:
Dear CPSC,
 
I have twin girls age 8 (they will be 9 in September of this year). The product that was gifted to them from my sister and purchased at Target can be found through the following link https://www.target.com/p/my-look-color-change-window-art-by-cra-z-art/-/A-76623847  and its for ages 6+
 
There is a stopper in each of the six window paints. This stopper pops up under compression (the only way to remove the stopper)  and splattered paint at a heavy force all over one my daughters face.  As she went to wash her face off and while in the shower the other twin handled another window paint and tried to remove the stopper by using the paint brush included in the kit, through adding pressure from the paint brush she that stopper released and popped right into her eye. It then forcefully ejected paint into her eye shutting her eye filled with paint. She cried hysterically in pain. My brother in law is an ER physician and I contacted him immediately. We then contacted poison control. My daughter had to irrigate her eyes for 15 minutes. That was the first two paints.
 
I saw there were four paints left. I looked at each one; they all had stoppers in them. I tried removing the stopper and there is no way to remove them without compressing the paint out but when you do the stopper forcefully ejects with paint. The reality is kids will look at it and try to pull them out and they cant pull them out when they do it ejects out forcefully. The only safe way to do this is to make sure the paint isnt facing you; grab a cup and push the stopper out with a cup. Thats what I had to do with each of them and I only knew to do this after hearing from kids what happened and being cautious of not facing the paint towards me. This item is extremely dangerous for children. It will easily injure a childs eye. 
 
Please recall this item immediately and dont wait for a child to lose their eye.
justification: The incident resulted in paint forcefully ejected into a child's eye, causing pain and requiring medical consultation and eye irrigation.

incident_description:
(11/20/2024) The consumer has a safety concern about a baby rattle that he purchased in New Mexico. Because of how it looked, the consumer checked online to see what  it was made did of. The online information also indicated that the toy is non-toxic. The consumer did a lead home test. The toy tested positive for lead.

The consumer also has some 15-year-old baby rattles that tested positive for lead.

Yes there was lead exposure injury.  Spoke with [REDACTED]" from "LP" Latin Percussion, he
confirmed balls are covered in a lead graphite and they have received similar calls about this concern.

incident_description: I purchased a suction-mount glass planter from Amazon that I was using to store small planted herbs on my kitchen window for a few months. One day I put a new plant in the planter and went to stick it back in place on the window. The design of the product requires a small amount of pressure applied in order for the suction cups to properly mount. Unfortunately this small amount of pressure was enough to cause the whole planter to shatter in my hand and plunge jagged glass into my right palm. I started bleeding profusely and rushed to urgent care, however they did not recommend stitching the wound until it had been evaluated by an orthopedic specialist at the emergency room. A few hours later I did receive six stitches and was scheduled for follow-up. Since then it has been determined that I most likely sustained nerve damage and will need to have surgery next week to repair the nerve that was cut.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring stitches and potential nerve damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the product failure led to injury under normal use conditions.

incident_description:
I am an experienced ceramics teacher and was using a Lockerbie kick wheel when my left finger was suddenly dragged into the crevice between the spinning wheel head and the surrounding splash pan. There was no room for my finger with the space only 1/4" between the spinning wheel and the metal surrounding splash pan. My finger is crushed badly and my wrist is sprained. I am in constant pain with these injuries and I have limited use of my left hand, which is the injured one.
Two of my students have since told me that a similar thing happened to them in the past, but they never told me: their fingers got caught between the wheel and the splash pan. One boy said he lost his finger nail. I'm sure that is the least that is going to result with my injury.
justification: The teacher suffered a crushed finger and sprained wrist, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident has occurred multiple times before, suggesting it is likely (4).

incident_description:
The consumer says that on 3/2/2009 he plugged the unit in to test it out.  It was working fine.  That same day he put the incubator into his shop building and filled it with eggs and one cup of water per the instructions.  On 3/3/09 he woke up to find his shop building on fire.  The building was still standing but everything inside was completely destroyed.    

He sent the retailer and the manufacturer an email on 3/19/2009 showing them photos and a description of what happened.  He did not receive a response. He tried to save some baby goats from the fire and suffered smoke inhalation.  He required medical treatment.  He was given a respirator treatment. He also had a portable respirator treatment until he could breathe normally again. 

The consumer received a letter notifying him of the recall on August 6th 2013 (Recall number: 13-085).  His product is part of this recall.
justification: The consumer suffered smoke inhalation requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). Fires caused by faulty equipment are possible but not frequent (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the pet product (cat house) has an overwhelming odor that while she was trying to put it together it made her feel ill.  She stated that she contacted the company and they advised that she would be reimbursed.  Caller stated that she had to discard the product due to the odor it emanated.

incident_description:
I experienced long-term chemical exposure from an unused chemistry lab kit made by Science Interactive. It was stored in its original box in a shared bedroom up on a shelf in the closet. Without my knowledge, the liquid chemicals were evaporating and forming gases, causing me respiratory issues for months starting around February 2023. I had it for a year and a half when the respiratory issues started because of the kit. I experienced coughing if I had been near where the kit was stored, such as sitting at my desk, and I would also get a burning sensation in my lungs. During these months the burning feeling would last around half an hour after leaving the area and would become a lighter irritation after more time passed. I noticed that the symptoms would only start when I was in my room around that area. Not knowing the cause, I got an air purifier for the desk, which didn't help. I also searched for mold, and I contacted a testing company. I suspected a chemical was causing the symptoms, but I didn't suspect the kit at that point because nothing inside had been opened. I was concerned and tried to avoid the area while also trying to figure out the cause. I then started to clean out the room. In May I emailed Science Interactive asking how to dispose of the unused lab kit.

On May 31st I opened the box and saw that the chemicals had been evaporating because there was little liquid in the bottles. I was scared but quickly took a few pictures to show a professor and then closed the box. Minutes later I started coughing and experiencing the familiar burning sensation, so I then knew this was what had been causing my respiratory issues. I messaged a professor and brought the kit to campus with the help of her instructions. Even after removing it, I continued to experience the burning sensation for many days. I emailed Science Interactive explaining the situation and asked to speak with someone about their product's safety or a chemistry expert. There were so many liquid chemicals in the kit that I was concerned not knowing what harmful chemicals could be formed with them evaporating and reacting with each other. The representative ignored my request and just said to dispose of the kit "to prevent further discomfort. This situation has been extremely upsetting. Science Interactive must disclose the possible gases that could be formed from the storage of the chemicals in their kit so that I know what health effects could result and can inform healthcare professionals.

Because there were no instructions for storage of the kit, I had asked the professor when I dropped the class if the unused kit could be kept longer. I originally intended to retake the class, and he told me it should be fine to still have it for if I was going to retake the class at a later semester. When I also asked again about it this year the professor said that similar bottles of chemicals were stored in the school lab for many semesters without problems and that the chemicals don't ordinarily age. I don't know if he could have anticipated that the chemicals werent sealed well, but I wouldn't have brought it into my home around me and my family if I had known. It was kept around room temperature, but it wasn't a strictly controlled environment, and there were no warnings that it needed to be. I'm very worried about what health effects this could have. After opening the kit and experiencing the burning sensation for days, I since have started having reoccurring acid reflux, something I didnt have before, along with increased lung sensitivity. I also have a hard swollen lymph node for months that I didnt have before. Representatives from both Science Interactive and the college didnt address my concerns, ignoring many of my questions or giving vague responses. This was difficult to write about because its such a shocking situation that has left me very shaken. I submitted a report in August when I found this site, but I asked to be able to rewrite it because I didnt submit it properly.

UPDATED ON 8/12/2024: [To update, this whole event has caused a lot of trauma and the lack of any kind of explanation or help has left me despondent. I have blamed myself for not taking more pictures of the contents of the box even though the kit was actively causing my lungs to burn, so my instinct was not to get closer and look at it more but to keep it away from myself and others. 
- The comment made by Science Interactive is false. I did have chemical exposure from the kit, and removing the kit stopped the burning lungs sensation and coughing. I was able to sit at the desk in the room again with no symptoms whatsoever after removing the kit. My symptoms improving after removing the kit from the area is detailed in medical records and also emails and texts with professors. I can provide these records. 
- TO BE CLEAR, I did NOT see every item in the kit as I very hastily took a picture of the material list, one of the bags of chemicals, and closed the lid again and then began to experience the burning and coughing minutes later. The mention by the manufacturer of "staining" in the box that I did not report is not something I can say was or wasn't there as I did not see everything in the box. Many items were covering each other, and I opened and closed the box as fast as I could. If something other than only just the chemicals themselves was involved, for example, the fuel burner or other item in the box, I completely admit I did not look at other items, as I was terrified and breathing the gas inside proved harmful because my lungs soon started burning after opening the box. I was in a state of panic. My instinct was not to go back to the box and look at everything when it was making my lungs burn. The fact that I did not look at each item is not proof that this did not happen. It did happen. I WISH it didn't. I thought at the time that the college or professors would do an investigation of the kit. In the moment, I was scared and trusting the professor to tell me exactly what to do and initially she said to throw the kit in the garbage, which didn't sound safe to me to put something actively giving off an unknown gas into the garbage that another person might pass by, so I asked if I could bring it to the college. She said to put it in a bag, so I did. She wasn't present at the campus, but I did as instructed and took it where she told me to.
- I have notified a total of two Chemistry professors about the long-term chemical exposure I experienced. Neither professor provided an explanation about what thing or things in the kit could have been the cause, even though I asked repeatedly. I also asked if the kit was investigated after I dropped it off at the school. This question was also ignored.
- I emailed the school board about what happened because the professors didn't provide me with any explanation. I thought the school would investigate, but the board did not respond to me at all. I said I didn't want to be ignored, and they ignored me. 
- The Consumer Product Safety Commission also has not contacted me further.   
- I took measurements of where the kit was on the shelf, how high off the ground, and measurements in relation to the desk I would sit at when I would start coughing, lungs burning. The kit was stored nearly 7 feet off the ground, and the gas was still reaching me despite that height. I have photos of the measurements and the room this was happening in. 
Measurements: 
* The box was stored on the highest shelf in the closet, 6 feet and 11 inches off the ground. 
* The chair I would sit at was around 5 feet and 6 inches over from where the box was stored.
* The height of the chair was around 3 feet and five inches from the ground. My head would be about a foot above this. 

I mentioned I found swollen lymph nodes following this prolonged exposure. One of them in particular is the most noticeable to me because it hurts daily from just everyday movements. The company's side comments about how long the kit was kept being "unusual" has no relevance to my report as there were NO instructions about the length of time it was safe to store. NONE. Not with the kit, not on their website. No student should experience chemical exposure due to your lack of proper instructions. I had dropped the class. Students drop classes all the time. I would not have kept it had there been anything detailing how long it was safe to keep. No student deserves to go through this. As for the comments that are outright lies, I will submit evidence to have them corrected or removed. The lesson on lab safety they keep mentioning also has no relevance. The box was stored, not used. The mention of lack of MSDS in my original report is to illustrate how carelessly this kit has been put together, but the fact that it was producing a gas that was causing me to cough and lungs to burn illustrates that well enough. Their comment that I did not state that the product caused issues in my emails is a lie. I will provide the emails to the CPSC.]
justification: The incident caused respiratory issues and other health effects, indicating injury.

incident_description: I began working with epoxy resin sold in Hobby Lobby and within a month I was having severe allergic reactions and highly increased number of health problems including extended menstrual bleeding and heavier than I have ever had in my life. The bleeding lasted for over 45 days straight. I had extreme facial swelling to the point I could barely open my eyes. Rash from head to toe and severe itching, drying of the skin and flaking/peeling of the skin in affected areas. Especially my eyes. Shortness of breath and labored breathing. I could not walk up a single flight of stairs without stopping to rest and catch my breath. No more than 50 feet at a time without resting. Increased sensitivity to common products that I had used for years prior to the exposure of BPA with no issues at all until now. Products such as hair shampoo and conditioners, soak off nail polishes and/or nail salon products and supplies, body wash, lotions, some makeups and a host of other products that I have come into contact with. Doctors were stumped and finally I convinced my PCP to allow me to get patch testing done for allergies. I was under the impression that I was allergic to topical alcohols. Turns out it was actually Bisphenol A and it's derivatives that I am severely allergic to since I began working with epoxy resins. My allergy level is rated between a 3 and 4 in severity. Since I was diagnosed, I have been trying to avoid contact with the products containing BPA or any related chemicals and am using BPA free epoxy and have had very little noted reactions. My health seems to be improving slowly and when I do come into contact with it, my health immediately worsens. I am trying to locate a list of common products that contain this chemical but am not having any luck. I believe that the gel nail polish or the activator contain some trace amounts of the chemical being that I had a slight reaction after applying it a few weeks back. I have to take an entire regimen of medications to reduce the effects of the reactions. They include [REDACTED] (my life saver that they do not like to give me, but really the only noticeable relief when taken) [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and [REDACTED] are the orally ingested products. Then for topical we have erythromycin ointment for my eyes which flake up and then ooze all around the eyelids, triamcinolone 0.1% ointment for the rest of my body that reacts as though I have severe eczema. I take [REDACTED] to stop the bleeding. There are also some eye drops I use to clear up the infection I get in my eyes. The whole thing is ridiculous and beyond irritating. I wish I had known the affects that this would take on me prior to trying the original product. I followed the recommended safety instructions and still this is where I am at. I am afraid to use so many products now out of fear that I will react to them. I would benefit greatly from a more detailed list of products that do or would be likely to contain this chemical so that I can try to resume a somewhat normal life like I had prior to the exposure. I would also be interested in being part of further research to examine more deeply the actual potential health issues that can occur from exposure to this chemical as I suspect that most of my recent health issues stem from this allergy. My Doctors are all looking beyond the obvious which is that I began experiencing 90% of my health complaints within a month of beginning use of the epoxy resin. Two plus two equals four....it seems fairly simple. Especially since the known effects include most of my health concerns. If anyone knows where I might find additional information on BPA or who to contact for studies that may be taking place, please let me know. I want to be a part of preventing others from having this happen to them!!!
justification: The description details severe allergic reactions and multiple health issues requiring medication, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific exposure to epoxy resin and subsequent reactions.

incident_description:
"Baby's First Book", Copyright 2011, reg# PA-15501, (CN), Style# 80189 and manufactured June 2012 in Dongguan, Guang Providence, China.

Book was received in November 2012 as shower gift.  Age range listed as 0+.

Mother received book as gift at shower in November 2012, her baby was born December 17, 2012.

She gave the book to her now six month old baby for the first time to play with about June 1st, 2013.

On Thursday, June 13th, 2013 the baby had only been playing with the book for a few moments when caller heard the baby begin screaming.

She ran to the baby to see what was wrong then noticed that the baby would not open her eyes.

She examined the baby's eye which was very red around the outside, the inside of the eye was watering.

She called the pediatrician who diagnosed a scratched cornea of the right eye then prescribed antibiotic eyedrops with artificial tears.

The caller/mother has taken the book away from the baby      

Caller contacted the manufacturer Friday, June 14th, 2013 and was advised to return it to their office.
